eng-nc-y1-plants-01.note: No lesson teaches identifying common wild and garden plants or deciduous and evergreen trees by name; u11-05 mentions deciduous forest only as a biome.

eng-nc-y1-plants-02.note: above: flower, root, stem and leaf structure are taught at secondary depth; the basic whole-plant structure of common flowering plants and trees for young children is not taught directly.

eng-nc-y1-animals-including-humans-01.note: No lesson teaches identifying and naming common fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.

eng-nc-y1-animals-including-humans-02.note: Herbivore, carnivore and omnivore appear as consumer roles in ecosystems; no lesson asks learners to identify and name common animals in each group.

eng-nc-y1-animals-including-humans-03.note: The animal kingdom's features are described; comparing the structure of fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals is not taught.

eng-nc-y1-animals-including-humans-04.note: Organ systems are outlined at secondary level; the senses and the body parts associated with each are not taught.

eng-nc-y2-living-things-and-their-habita.note: above: taught as the characteristics of life and hard cases; "dead" versus "never alive" is covered by applying the characteristics.
Habitat and niche, adaptation and interdependence are taught at secondary depth; meeting the basic needs of animals and plants in named habitats is not taught for this age.
No lesson asks learners to identify and name plants and animals in habitats or microhabitats.
above: food chains are taught fully; naming different sources of food for animals is not taught.

eng-nc-y2-plants-01.note: Germination and asexual reproduction (bulbs) are taught; observing seeds and bulbs growing into mature plants is not a lesson activity.

eng-nc-y2-plants-02.note: Water and temperature for germination, and light for photosynthesis, are taught; what plants need to grow and stay healthy is not drawn together.

eng-nc-y2-animals-including-humans-01.note: Human growth and development after birth are described; animals having offspring that grow into adults is not taught as a general idea for this age.

eng-nc-y2-animals-including-humans-02.note: Nutrition and respiration as characteristics of life imply the needs; the basic needs of animals (water, food and air) are not taught directly.

eng-nc-y2-animals-including-humans-03.note: No lesson teaches the importance of exercise, a balanced diet and hygiene for health.

eng-nc-y3-plants-01.note: above: roots, stems, leaves and flowers are each a lesson at secondary depth.

eng-nc-y3-plants-02.note: Mineral nutrients and the conditions for germination and photosynthesis are taught; room to grow and variation between plants is not.

eng-nc-y3-plants-03.note: above: water transport, xylem and transpiration (with a potometer) are taught.

eng-nc-y3-plants-04.note: above: pollination, seed formation and dispersal are taught.

eng-nc-y3-animals-including-humans-01.note: Digestion of food and the consumer role are taught; the right types and amounts of nutrition (a balanced diet) are not.

eng-nc-y3-animals-including-humans-02.note: above: functions of the skeleton and antagonistic muscles.

eng-nc-y4-living-things-and-their-habita.note: above: taught as taxonomy and the kingdoms.
No lesson teaches using or constructing classification (dichotomous) keys.
above: climate change, habitat fragmentation and pollution as threats are taught at secondary depth.

eng-nc-y4-animals-including-humans-01.note: above: organs of the digestive system and their roles.

eng-nc-y4-animals-including-humans-02.note: No lesson teaches the types of human teeth and their functions.

eng-nc-y4-animals-including-humans-03.note: Food chains and webs are taught fully; predator and prey in u11-17.

eng-nc-y5-living-things-and-their-habita.note: No lesson compares the life cycles of a mammal, an amphibian, an insect and a bird; u11-19 covers parasite life cycles only.
above: sexual and asexual reproduction in plants, and human reproduction and fertilisation.

eng-nc-y5-animals-including-humans-01.note: Growth and development after birth is taught; changes through to old age are only touched on (cellular senescence).

eng-nc-y6-living-things-and-their-habita.note: above: classification into kingdoms and domains, including micro-organisms.
above: classifying an unfamiliar organism from its features.

eng-nc-y6-animals-including-humans-01.note: above: the circulatory system, heart, vessels and blood each have a lesson.

eng-nc-y6-animals-including-humans-02.note: Cardiovascular risk factors, exercise and smoking are touched on; diet, drugs and lifestyle as a whole are not taught.

eng-nc-y6-animals-including-humans-03.note: above: circulation, absorption and tissue fluid.

eng-nc-y6-evolution-and-inheritance-01.note: above: fossil formation, dating and what fossils show.

eng-nc-ks3-cells-and-organisation-01.note: Cell theory and light microscopy, including magnification; recording cell structure from a slide is not a practical activity in the course.

eng-nc-ks3-cells-and-organisation-05.note: Protozoa and prokaryote structure are taught; structural adaptations of unicellular organisms (e.g. Euglena, amoeba) are not drawn together.

eng-nc-ks3-the-skeletal-and-muscular-sys.note: Bone marrow making blood cells is in u07-28 and u02-26.
Joints, levers and antagonistic pairs are taught; measuring the force exerted by different muscles is not.

eng-nc-ks3-nutrition-and-digestion-01.note: The biomolecules and their digestion are taught; a healthy diet, and why vitamins, minerals, fibre and water are needed, are not.

eng-nc-ks3-nutrition-and-digestion-02.note: No lesson teaches calculating daily energy requirements from diet.

eng-nc-ks3-nutrition-and-digestion-03.note: Obesity, starvation and deficiency diseases from diet are not taught (u08-11 covers mineral deficiencies in plants only).

eng-nc-ks3-gas-exchange-systems-02.note: Inspiration and expiration with pressure changes, and lung volumes.

eng-nc-ks3-gas-exchange-systems-03.note: Respiratory diseases including asthma, and smoking, are taught; the effect of exercise on the gas exchange system is only touched on.

eng-nc-ks3-reproduction-01.note: Maternal lifestyle effects on the foetus via the placenta are covered in u07-32.

eng-nc-ks3-reproduction-02.note: Quantitative investigation of dispersal mechanisms is not taught.

eng-nc-ks3-health-01.note: Alcohol and nicotine appear only as risks in pregnancy; the effects of recreational drugs and substance misuse on behaviour and health are not taught.

eng-nc-ks3-photosynthesis-02.note: Photosynthesis as the base of food chains, energy flow and the carbon cycle; oxygen levels in the atmosphere are touched on.

eng-nc-ks3-cellular-respiration-01.note: Aerobic respiration is located in mitochondria and anaerobic respiration is taught for plants; no lesson teaches respiration in living organisms as a whole, including in animals.

eng-nc-ks3-cellular-respiration-02.note: The respiration equation appears in plant respiration; no lesson teaches the word summary for aerobic respiration as such.

eng-nc-ks3-cellular-respiration-03.note: Anaerobic respiration in plants and fermentation by microbes are taught; anaerobic respiration in humans (lactic acid) is not.

eng-nc-ks3-cellular-respiration-04.note: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration are compared for plants only; implications for humans are not taught.

eng-nc-ks3-relationships-in-an-ecosystem.note: The importance of pollinators is taught; their role in human food security is not drawn out explicitly.
Biomagnification of toxic materials and pollution.

eng-nc-ks3-inheritance-chromosomes-dna-a.note: Includes the X-ray work of Franklin and Wilkins and the Watson–Crick model.
What a species is, and speciation, are taught; differences between species are not a lesson focus.
Continuous and discontinuous variation; graphs of variation in u01-17.
Gene banks and seed banks as ex-situ conservation.

eng-aqa8461-4.1.1.1.note: Order-of-magnitude size comparisons are in u01-14 and u01-16.

eng-aqa8461-4.1.1.2.note: Required practical 1 (observing cells with a light microscope) is described, not carried out.

eng-aqa8461-4.1.1.6.note: Required practical 2 (antibiotic inhibition zones) is described in outline only.

eng-aqa8461-4.1.2.3.note: Therapeutic cloning is touched on; meristem cloning of plants in u08-34.

eng-aqa8461-4.1.3.1.note: Surface area to volume ratio and exchange surfaces in gas exchange, the gut and leaves.

eng-aqa8461-4.1.3.2.note: Required practical 3 (osmosis in plant tissue) is described, not carried out.

eng-aqa8461-4.2.2.1.note: Food tests (required practical 4) and enzyme rate (required practical 5) are described; bile emulsifying fat is in u07-23.

eng-aqa8461-4.2.2.4.note: Coronary heart disease and its risk factors are taught; treatments (stents, statins, valve replacement, transplants, artificial hearts) are not evaluated.

eng-aqa8461-4.2.2.5.note: No lesson defines health or explains how communicable and non-communicable diseases interact, or how diet, stress and life situations affect health.

eng-aqa8461-4.2.2.6.note: Risk factors for cardiovascular disease and cancer, and correlation versus causation, are taught; the effects of diet, smoking and alcohol on specific organs, and use of risk data, are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.1.2.note: Viral structure and HIV are taught; measles and tobacco mosaic virus as named GCSE examples are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.1.3.note: Bacterial disease is taught; Salmonella and gonorrhoea as named examples, and poultry vaccination, are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.1.4.note: Fungal pathogens are taught in general; rose black spot and its treatment are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.1.5.note: Malaria and mosquito vectors are taught.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.1.6.note: Includes physical barriers, phagocytosis and antibodies; antitoxins are not named.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.1.8.note: Painkillers (which treat symptoms, not the cause) are not taught.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.1.9.note: Drug discovery stages and placebo controls are taught; digitalis, aspirin and penicillin origins and the phases of clinical trials (double-blind) are not drawn together.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.2.2.note: Therapeutic and diagnostic uses are taught; pregnancy tests and the side effects of monoclonal antibodies are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.3.1.note: Detecting and identifying plant diseases, and ion deficiencies (nitrate, magnesium) as plant conditions, are not taught; u08-11 covers mineral deficiency symptoms only in part.

eng-aqa8461-4.3.3.2.note: Plant stress responses are taught; physical, chemical and mechanical defences against pathogens and herbivores are not covered as such.

eng-aqa8461-4.4.1.2.note: Limiting factors; the inverse square law and greenhouse economics (HT) are not taught; required practical 6 described in outline.

eng-aqa8461-4.4.1.3.note: Starch, cellulose, respiration and nitrate for amino acids are covered across lessons; uses of glucose are not drawn together.

eng-aqa8461-4.4.2.1.note: Aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration in plants and fermentation are taught; anaerobic respiration in muscles (lactic acid) is not.

eng-aqa8461-4.4.2.2.note: Blood flow and breathing during exercise are touched on; oxygen debt and lactic acid in muscles are not taught.

eng-aqa8461-4.4.2.3.note: Metabolic reactions (polymers, lipid synthesis, amino acids, urea) are taught across lessons; metabolism is not drawn together.

eng-aqa8461-4.5.2.1.note: Required practical 7 (reaction time) is not described.

eng-aqa8461-4.5.2.2.note: Methods of studying the brain and the difficulty of treating brain disorders are touched on only.

eng-aqa8461-4.5.2.3.note: No lesson teaches the structure of the eye, accommodation or the correction of myopia and hyperopia.

eng-aqa8461-4.5.3.3.note: Includes deamination, ADH, dialysis and transplants.

eng-aqa8461-4.5.3.6.note: IVF and fertility drugs are described.

eng-aqa8461-4.5.3.7.note: Adrenaline and thyroxine in negative feedback.

eng-aqa8461-4.5.4.1.note: Required practical 8 (light or gravity on seedlings) is described in outline only.

eng-aqa8461-4.6.1.3.note: Sexual versus asexual reproduction in plants; malaria parasites and fungi reproducing both ways are touched on.

eng-aqa8461-4.6.1.7.note: Cystic fibrosis is taught; polydactyly and embryo screening, with its economic, social and ethical issues, are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.6.2.3.note: Selective breeding is mentioned only as traditional biotechnology; its process, uses and the risks of inbreeding are not taught.

eng-aqa8461-4.6.2.5.note: Plant cuttings and tissue culture are taught, and adult cell cloning (Dolly) is mentioned; embryo transplants are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.6.3.6.note: Extinction and its causes are taught across lessons; not drawn together as one topic.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.2.1.note: Predator-prey cycles in u11-17; required practical 9 (quadrats and transects) in u01-19.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.2.3.note: Decomposers are taught; the effect of temperature, water and oxygen on decay, compost and biogas, and required practical 10, are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.3.3.note: Habitat loss is taught; destruction of peat bogs and burning peat are not.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.3.4.note: Deforestation's effect on carbon dioxide and biodiversity is mentioned; reasons for deforestation (cattle, rice, biofuels) are not taught.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.3.6.note: Breeding programmes, habitat protection and hedgerows.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.5.1.note: Sustainability of food production is taught; the factors threatening food security (new pests, conflict, cost of farming) are not taught as a topic.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.5.2.note: Energy loss between trophic levels underpins it; intensive farming of animals and its ethics are not taught.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.5.3.note: Fishing quotas and net mesh size.

eng-aqa8461-4.7.5.4.note: Mycoprotein in u09-29; GM crops including golden rice in u08-34.

eng-edx1bi0-1.2.note: Sperm and egg adaptations; ciliated epithelial cells are not named.

eng-edx1bi0-1.6.note: Core practical: magnification calculations and the microscope are taught; the practical itself is described, not carried out.

eng-edx1bi0-1.10.note: Core practical: how to investigate enzyme activity is described.

eng-edx1bi0-1.12.note: Enzymes as catalysts and digestion are taught; enzymes in the synthesis of carbohydrates, proteins and lipids are only implied.

eng-edx1bi0-1.13B.note: Food tests with chemical reagents (iodine, Benedict's, biuret, emulsion test) are not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-1.14B.note: Measuring the energy in food by calorimetry is not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-1.16.note: Core practical: osmosis in plant tissue is described.

eng-edx1bi0-1.17.note: Percentage change in mass is not worked through.

eng-edx1bi0-2.5.note: Growth by division and differentiation in animals, and elongation and meristems in plants, are taught in separate lessons.

eng-edx1bi0-2.7.note: Percentile charts for monitoring growth are not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-2.11B.note: Brain imaging (CT and PET scanning) is mentioned at most in passing.

eng-edx1bi0-2.12B.note: Limits to treating nervous-system damage and disease are not drawn out.

eng-edx1bi0-2.15B.note: No lesson teaches the structure and function of the eye.

eng-edx1bi0-2.16B.note: Eye defects (cataracts, long- and short-sightedness, colour blindness) are not taught; colour blindness appears only as an X-linked example in u04-27.

eng-edx1bi0-2.17B.note: Correcting eye defects is not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-3.6.note: Nucleic acid extraction is described as a laboratory technique; extracting DNA from fruit is not.

eng-edx1bi0-4.5.note: Human evolution is taught; dating stone tools is not drawn out.

eng-edx1bi0-4.8.note: Selective breeding is mentioned only as traditional biotechnology; there is no lesson on it.

eng-edx1bi0-4.13B.note: Fertilisers and biological control are taught; their advantages and disadvantages as agricultural solutions are not drawn together.

eng-edx1bi0-4.14.note: Benefits and risks of genetic engineering are taught; selective breeding is not.

eng-edx1bi0-5.2.note: Communicable disease is taught; the contrast with non-communicable disease is not.

eng-edx1bi0-5.3.note: Immunodeficiency increasing susceptibility (HIV) is taught; disease interactions in general are not.

eng-edx1bi0-5.5.note: Cholera, tuberculosis, Chalara ash dieback, malaria and HIV are covered across lessons; Helicobacter stomach ulcers and Ebola are mentioned only in passing.

eng-edx1bi0-5.8.note: STIs as a group (chlamydia, HIV) and their prevention are not drawn together.

eng-edx1bi0-5.9B.note: Physical defences of plants against pathogens and pests are not taught as such.

eng-edx1bi0-5.10B.note: Chemical defences of plants are not taught as such.

eng-edx1bi0-5.11B.note: Molecular diagnostics are taught for humans; detecting and identifying plant diseases is not.

eng-edx1bi0-5.18B.note: Core practical on antiseptics and antibiotics is described in outline only.

eng-edx1bi0-5.19B.note: Calculating the area of inhibition zones with πr² is not worked through.

eng-edx1bi0-5.20.note: Discovery is taught; the testing phases (preclinical, clinical trials, double-blind) are not drawn together.

eng-edx1bi0-5.22B.note: Diagnostic and therapeutic uses are taught; pregnancy testing is not.

eng-edx1bi0-5.23.note: Multifactorial causes of cardiovascular disease and cancer are taught separately.

eng-edx1bi0-5.24.note: Lifestyle risk factors are mentioned; their effects at local, national and global levels are not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-5.25.note: Treatments for cardiovascular disease (medication, surgery, lifestyle) are not evaluated.

eng-edx1bi0-6.5.note: Core practical on light intensity is described in outline.

eng-edx1bi0-6.6.note: The inverse square law for light intensity is not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-7.8.note: IVF is taught; clomifene therapy is not named.

eng-edx1bi0-7.17.note: Correlation is taught; BMI and waist:hip calculations are not.

eng-edx1bi0-8.2.note: Surface area to volume ratio calculations.

eng-edx1bi0-8.9.note: Respiration releasing energy for ATP is taught; respiration as a continuous exothermic process in all cells is not drawn together.

eng-edx1bi0-8.10.note: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration are compared for plants only.

eng-edx1bi0-8.11.note: The core practical on the rate of respiration (respirometers) is not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-9.5.note: Core practical: quadrats and transects are described.

eng-edx1bi0-9.9.note: Invasive species, pollution, conservation; fish farming is touched on in u11-30.

eng-edx1bi0-9.11B.note: Food security factors are not drawn together as a topic.

eng-edx1bi0-9.14.note: The water cycle is taught; producing potable water (including desalination) is not.

eng-edx1bi0-9.17B.note: Food preservation is mentioned; the effects of temperature, water and oxygen on food decay are not taught.

eng-edx1bi0-9.18B.note: Decomposers are taught; factors affecting the rate of decomposition in composting are not.

eng-edx1bi0-9.19B.note: Calculating rates of decay is not taught.
